subject: Uptime tally question: partial degradation during 2025-07-14 maintenance window
messages:
From: Elaine Harper <elaine.harper@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: techops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime calculation dispute for 2025-07-14 partial degradation

Marcus —

Thanks for taking a look. On 2025-07-14 we saw a 75-minute period between 03:10 and 04:25 UTC where our API traffic experienced elevated error rates and 500ms+ tail latency across a subset of endpoints. Nimbus Health relies on your API for real-time patient triage; this window materially affected our throughput and triggered internal incident reviews.

Your support portal ticket (ID 45789) says the event was treated as a third-party CDN incident and excluded from Redwood uptime calculations, which resulted in no SLA credit. We disagree with the exclusion — the degradation was partial (some requests succeeded, others failed) and overlapped with your scheduled maintenance window by ~20 minutes. Our contract SLO language indicates partial degradation that increases error rate/latency beyond the 99th percentile should contribute to downtime calculations.

We need:
- A clear explanation of how Redwood computed the uptime for 2025-07-14 and why the 75-minute window was excluded in full.
- The specific rule in the SLA or SLO doc applied in this case.
- Any logs/traces you can share so we can correlate with our data.

If the current interpretation stands, we will request formal credit and potentially escalate to procurement. Please advise next steps and an expected timeline for a formal review.

Attachments: none in this email (we attached our incident summary to ticket 45789).

Best,
Elaine Harper
Director, Platform Reliability
Nimbus Health

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear summary and for flagging this. I’m escalating this internally and opening a formal SLO review.

Short answers up front: we do exclude incidents attributable solely to third-party infrastructure from Redwood-hosted uptime, but we do include partial degradations where our serving layer contributed materially. From the ticket notes we saw the initial classification was CDN-limited; that said, I don’t want to close the door until we’ve correlated traces.

Marissa and Neha — can you pull the SLO windowing calc for Nimbus’ account, the raw token-level success/latency curves for 2025-07-14 02:30–05:00 UTC, and the routing decision logs? Elaine, I’ll share those artifacts when ready.

Proposed timeline: internal review today, preliminary response by EOD PDT, and a proposed credit calculation by Monday 07/21 if we concur a credit is warranted. If not, we’ll provide the precise rationale and data.

Thanks — Marcus
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Uptime calculation dispute for 2025-07-14 partial degradation

Forwarding the customer note. Quick internal read: our SLO calc uses token-weighted uptime with a 5-minute bucketing and a 99.9% availability target. Per policy we exclude windows where external providers report an independent outage AND our routing shows zero dropped requests. But here the customer reports sustained error-rate increase and >500ms tail; that suggests partial impact inside our runtime or at the edge.

Action items for this thread (Marcus owns customer comms):
- I pulled the token-level per-route latency histogram (attached as slo-report-2025-07-14.csv). It shows a clear bump starting 03:08 UTC and tapering at ~04:28 UTC, with a 99.9th percentile jump from 180ms to 920ms.
- We also have a pcap excerpt from the edge layer showing increased retransmits (network-trace-2025-07-14.pcap). Not definitive of CDN vs our infra yet.
- Suggest we run a correlation: CDN status logs vs our edge latency and origin CPU. If both show impact, we should treat this as eligible for SLO adjustment/credit.

Proposed customer-facing language: acknowledge impact, commit to a joint investigation, deliver preliminary credit estimate (based on token-weighted downtime) and offer a technical postmortem call.

Marissa
Sr. Director, Reliability Engineering
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime calculation dispute for 2025-07-14 partial degradation

Copying relevant notes from the SLO playbook:
- We compute availability per-tenant as: 1 - (sum_downtime_tokens / total_tokens_in_period). Downtime tokens accrue when latency > SLA_latency_threshold OR error_rate > SLA_error_threshold within a bucket.
- Maintenance windows are excluded only if pre-declared in the tenant's maintenance calendar and if the impact is attributable exclusively to planned maintenance executed by Redwood.
- Third-party exclusions require corroborating third-party incident records AND confirmation our routing shows 0 errors.

From the preliminary traces: our origin CPU stayed within baseline, but edge retransmits coincide with an AS-level route flap reported by CDN provider at 03:12–03:42 UTC. However, our edge processed a non-trivial number of 5xx responses during 03:10–03:30 UTC. That indicates the event was not purely a CDN blackhole — there's shared responsibility.

Given this, I recommend we:
1) Offer a conditional credit equal to the token-weighted downtime during the 03:10–04:25 UTC window (prelim calc attached).
2) Schedule a joint postmortem call with Nimbus and the CDN provider; include network ops and account leads.
3) Update the incident classification to "shared external/edge degradation" and re-run SLO calc with partial attribution.

I'll finish a verified token-weighted calculation and hand it to Marcus to share.

Neha
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Harper <elaine.harper@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: techops@nimbushealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uptime calculation dispute for 2025-07-14 partial degradation

Elaine — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary and next steps below.

What we found:
- Attachments included: slo-report-2025-07-14.csv (token-weighted latency histogram) and network-trace-2025-07-14.pcap (edge-level packet capture excerpt).
- The event spanned ~03:08–04:28 UTC on 2025-07-14.
- CDN provider reported an AS route flap 03:12–03:42 UTC. Our edge saw increased retransmits and a non-trivial number of 5xx responses 03:10–03:30 UTC. Origin CPU and model-serving kernels were within normal ranges.

Interpretation:
- This was a shared-impact incident: partial degradation where both CDN routing instability and edge-layer retransmits contributed to user-visible errors/latency. Under our SLO policy (section 4.2), full third-party exclusions are only applied when (a) we have a third-party incident record and (b) our routing/edge metrics show zero errors. Neither condition held. Therefore we will not exclude the entire window.

Proposed remediation/credit:
- We propose a provisional credit equal to token-weighted downtime for the 03:10–04:25 UTC window, which equates to 4.2% of Nimbus’ billed tokens for the monthly cycle (prelim). We can apply that as a one-time usage credit against your August invoice or as a billable SLA credit, whichever you prefer.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you’d like the credit applied to August invoice or as an SLA billing credit.
2) We propose a joint postmortem on Wed 07/23 at 10:00 AM EDT — Marcus, Marissa, Neha and our CDN contact will join. Elaine, does that work?
3) We will publish a short incident note in the tenant portal after the postmortem.

If you want more granular breakdown before the postmortem, we can provide a per-endpoint token-weighted table.

Regards,
Marcus
